messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — API ref for POST /chat.stream has inconsistent usage of the message field. Examples in the JS snippet use `speaker` instead of `role`. I opened a tiny PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412

docbot: PR created: docs#412 by maya — running docs CI :github: (status: pending)

luis: Confirmed. JS snippet sends `messages: [{speaker: 'user', content: '...'}]` but the request schema expects `role` enum (`user`|`assistant`|`system`). That will break TS typing and some client validation.

irene: Also noticed the streaming response example lists `delta: {content: '...'}` but real responses sometimes include `delta: {role: 'assistant', content: '...'}` on the first chunk. Schema should allow `role` optional in delta.

sam: Plan: 1) update all SDK and curl examples to use `role`, 2) add a small note about optional `role` in streaming deltas, 3) add a tiny migration note for older clients. I can push commits to the PR later today. :+1:

maya: I pushed an initial change swapping `speaker` -> `role` in the JS and Python snippets. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/abc123def

luis: Small nit in the curl example — it's currently double-encoding the JSON (we have `-d '{"messages": "[{...}]"}'`). That frequently confuses folks. Suggest this minimal curl form instead:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/chat.stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "rwd-chat-1",
    "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]
  }'
```

irene: One more: the Go SDK snippet still defines `type Message struct { Speaker string }`. I'll open a follow-up PR to rename to `Role string` and add a comment about allowed values.

docbot: CI passed for docs#412 and docs#413, merge queue clear — will auto-merge on approval.

maya: Thanks all — merging now. I'll add a short changelog entry mentioning the example corrections and the streaming delta schema clarification.
